hero.title: Prehistory: Geography and Characteristics
hero.description: A comprehensive analysis of Paleolithic, Mesolithic, and Neolithic settlements and their ecological determinants in the Indian subcontinent.

timeline.title: The Chronological Framework
timeline.description: Evolutionary stages of human life in India based on stone technology.

cards.details: Development of Hand-axe and Cleaver industries (Soan and Madrasian cultures).
Transition period; shift to microlithic tools and hunter-gatherer to incipient farming.
Sedentary life, agriculture, pottery, and polished stone tools.

mnemonics.title: Mnemonics & Tricks
mnemonics.description: Memory aids for major regional sites.

items.title: B.A.D. - Site Clusters
items.decryption: These represent the core Paleolithic zones: MP (Bhimbetka), TN (Attirampakkam), and Rajasthan (Didwana).

traps.title: UPSC Common Exam Traps
items: Confusing Microliths exclusively with Neolithic (They are markers of Mesolithic).
Assuming Indus Valley is the starting point of Indian history (Prehistory precedes it by thousands of years).
Thinking copper tools (Chalcolithic) replaced stone immediately; they co-existed for centuries.

deepDive.title: Syllabus Core Study Notes (Deep-Dive)
deepDive.description: Master the spatial mapping, site categorizations, raw material networks, and cultural-environmental characteristics of Indian prehistory.

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Geography

  • Sites near perennial rivers
  • Cave shelters (Vindhyas)
  • Alluvial plains vs Plateau

Characteristics

  • Tool technology evolution
  • Food gathering to producing
  • Rock art depictions
PeriodTool TypeKey Site
PaleolithicCore ToolsBhimbetka
MesolithicMicrolithsBagor
NeolithicPolished StoneMehrgarh
  • Paleolithic: Food gathering; Soan Valley (Punjab) and Madrasian culture.
  • Mesolithic: Fishing & Hunting; Bagor (Rajasthan) and Adamgarh (MP).
  • Neolithic: Domestication; Mehrgarh (Balochistan) evidence of wheat/barley.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following represents the core geo-archaeological feature of the prehistoric site of Attirampakkam (Practice Q0)?
opts: earliest Acheulian tool assembly dating to >1.5 MYA
Urban town planning with grid street system
practiceQuestions.sol: The site of Attirampakkam is defined primarily by its Lower Paleolithic Acheulian characteristics.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following represents the core geo-archaeological feature of the prehistoric site of Bhimbetka (Practice Q1)?
opts: continuous habitation and prehistoric rock shelters
Urban town planning with grid street system
practiceQuestions.sol: The site of Bhimbetka is defined primarily by its Paleolithic to Mesolithic rock art characteristics.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following represents the core geo-archaeological feature of the prehistoric site of Mehrgarh (Practice Q2)?
opts: earliest farming, wheat-barley cultivation and cattle herding
Urban town planning with grid street system
practiceQuestions.sol: The site of Mehrgarh is defined primarily by its Neolithic to Chalcolithic transition characteristics.

mockTestQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the prehistoric geography (Mock Q0):
1. Attirampakkam is located in Tamil Nadu.
2. It yields evidence of earliest Acheulian tool assembly dating to >1.5 MYA.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct based on the geographical distribution mapping of Attirampakkam.
